findings.text: The task folder has no `requirements.md` (the file this review was told to read), no `task.jsonl` and no outcome. What was approved lives only in one `session.jsonl` log line ("report section 7 items 1-6" plus an extras list). A fresh agent can't tell from this folder what was asked, what is done, or that the work sits unmerged on `worktree/qf-2` (commits ad482eb59, 8fcd09ffc). Write the brief and a short status note into the folder.

Approved item 4 is only half done. A ready pool slot no longer holds a browser (`Servex/Pool.js:530`, `:588`), but whisper-server and the recite python still have no idle stop, and "only the newest tunnel per name" was not built: `Server/Tunnel.mjs:42` only blocks a second launch. `Servex/doc/processes.md:1000` calls this "an open improvement", but there is no task or `⬜` line for it anywhere.

Landing now removes the worktree the landing agent may still be working in. `Server/merge.mjs:96` and `Lifecycle.closeout` (called by `on-landing.mjs:117`) call `Worktrees.close_now`, and `close_now` (`Servex/Worktrees.js:615`) never checks `agent_in()`; in merge.mjs the Worktrees object has no `agents` to check anyway. On Windows, a cwd inside the folder lets `git worktree remove` delete the files but not the folder, leaving the agent in a gutted checkout. Refuse when an agent or the calling process has its cwd inside the folder, and report that case as `left`.

`Servex/doc/lifecycle.md` is now stale. Line 27 says on-landing calls `reap(task)` (it now calls `closeout`). Line 39 says "a worktree's files are never deleted by the reaper… removing the folder stays with worktree-sweep.mjs" (closeout now removes merged worktrees and moves leftover folders aside). The CLI list at line 51 lacks `--closeout`. Nothing there mentions the launcher-gone rule or the launcher kill.

Other docs the diff touches are stale too. `Servex/doc/pool.md:5` still says a ready slot has "a page watcher on", but it now starts on take. `Server/doc/browser.md:5` doesn't mention `browser-watchdog.mjs` or `LEW_NO_BROWSER_WATCHDOG`. `Server/doc/scripts.md` lists neither `Server/browser-watchdog.mjs` nor `Servex/closeout.test.mjs`. merge.mjs's header usage line (`Server/merge.mjs:1`) lacks `--keep-worktree` and the new auto-removal. `Servex/doc/task-loop.md:47` describes `close_task({dir, why})` without the close-out or `by`.

`Lifecycle.kill` (`Servex/Lifecycle.js:333-336`) now also kills a browser's launcher node.exe unless its command line matches Servex/claude/mcp/vscode. A long-lived process that holds a Playwright browser in-process could have its server killed along with its browser: the main dev server's `Server/plugins/Shot.js` is one such process, and its browser has no owner task in the main checkout, so it would be swept after 2 h. Shot.js closes its browser on every call, so today the risk is small. An allow-list of short-lived scripts would be safer than a deny-list.

The report left one question open: does the live sweep actually close things (`report.md` §3.2, §7.1)? The task folder never says whether that was settled. The retry on an empty process list (`Lifecycle.js:222`) may be the answer; say so in the folder.

`finish-task` (`.claude/skills/finish-task/SKILL.md:9`) tells the agent to read `left`, but nothing refuses a landing when `left` is not empty. `on-landing.mjs:118` only appends "LEFT: …". The report's §5 proposed a refusal; if a log line is enough, write that decision down.
`worktree-up.mjs:182` now records an owner, but `start_server` (approved item 6) was not changed. Hand-started servers through Servex still carry `owner_task: null`.
Simpler to read: `merge.mjs:97-99` imports `Servex/Lifecycle.js` twice in a row. The good part: `Servex/closeout.test.mjs` is real, rerunnable proof, using real processes, git and disk.

findings.text: The not-built items (idle unload of whisper/recite, newest tunnel per name, `start_server` carrying the caller) are said to be "recorded in [improvements](/Servex/improvements.jsonl)" (requirements.md items 4 and 6, review.jsonl answer 9), but `Servex/improvements.jsonl` does not exist on `worktree/qf-2`, in the qf-2 folder, or on compliance/dev. Those three asks are not written down anywhere, and the link is dead.

The proof leaves a footprint: `git worktree list` still shows `worktrees/closeout-test-bigjys` and `closeout-test-qt4dmy`, with their branches, from runs that never reached the test's `finally`. `Servex/closeout.test.mjs` should remove leftover `closeout-test-*` worktrees and branches when it starts.

`Lifecycle.kill()` (Servex/Lifecycle.js, the new launcher kill after `kill(r)`) also kills a browser's launching node process, and only exempts the main checkout. `Server/plugins/Shot.js` and `MCP.js` open browsers inside a worktree's own dev server, so when that browser is closed (for example by the new rule "a ready pool slot holds no browser"), the slot's dev server is killed too, even though `kept()` protects it. Exempt `server.js`/`run.js` launchers, not just the main path.

In `Lifecycle.why()`, the new "launcher is gone" rule sits before `if (only)`. So one task's `closeout` closes other tasks' orphan browsers, and if one survives the kill, its re-check lists it in this task's `left`.

`Worktrees.list()` now returns every linked worktree, wherever it is, including ones a Claude Code tab makes under `.claude/worktrees/`. The header comment (Servex/Worktrees.js:14-18, "Every folder in C:/Code/lew42/worktrees/") is now stale.

`Pool.generated()` treats any tracked `*.jsonl` edited in place as machine-written. An agent's uncommitted edit to a tracked log (asks.jsonl, a task.jsonl) is put back to HEAD on return and survives only as a patch in `.worktree-logs/`. Say so in Servex/doc/pool.md.

Indexing: `Servex/closeout.test.mjs` is listed in Server/doc/scripts.md's `Server/` table. `Servex/closeout.fixture.mjs` and the state file `worktree-sweep-fails.json` are not named in any doc (processes.md only says "state in the Servex state folder").

findings.text: The task folder doesn't mention this follow-up. The change is commit 3f5d9f788 on `worktree/qf-8` and is not merged into compliance/dev, yet `requirements.md` still says "Status: built, reviewed and merged (c3a59f3ba)" and has no line for this work. A fresh agent can't tell from the folder that the change exists or that it is waiting to merge. Add a deliverable line that names the branch and its state.

Two docs now describe the old behaviour. `requirements.md:9` says the list "is retried once", and `requirements.md:21` says the test has "11 checks" (it now has 12). `Servex/doc/processes.md:43` says "it is now retried once", which contradicts line 31 of the same file, now "retries twice".

A closeout that can't read the process list still goes on to remove worktrees (`Servex/Lifecycle.js` closeout loop → `Worktrees.close_now`). With an empty list, `close_under` and `held_by` see no processes inside the folder, so a dev server running in a merged worktree goes unseen and the removal can be only partly done. The final report still says `ok: false` with the cause, so nothing is hidden. Skipping the worktree step when `!this.procs?.size` would be the safer choice.

When PowerShell answers but `netstat` fails, the error is dropped (`process_error` is set only when the map is empty, `Lifecycle.js` `processes_async`). The listing then has no ports, and nothing says why.
The commit message says "retried three times", but the code makes three attempts, which is two retries. `processes.md:31` gets this right ("retries twice, after 1.5 s, then 3 s").

It works: I ran `node Servex/closeout.test.mjs` on `worktree/qf-8` and got "ALL 12 CHECKS PASSED", with 0 test processes and 0 test worktrees left at cleanup. The new check fakes `processes_async`, which is the simplest honest way to test this. Guarding `sweep`'s "found gone" lines with `this.procs?.size` is the right minimal fix: an unreadable list used to mark every live process dead.

The task folder does not record this change: `requirements.md` ends at deliverable 8 (still "merge recorded below once landed", with no merge line) and says nothing about the Crumbs cause, branch `worktree/qf-2` or commit 0a403a6b0. A fresh agent reading this folder would not know the real cause of the empty process list was found, or that it still has to be merged. Add a deliverable 9 with the branch, the test and the merge once it lands.

The Crumbs module's own doc is now stale. `Servex/doc/restart.md:34` and `:52` describe `Crumbs.js`, but neither says it must keep `util.promisify.custom`. The new test `Servex/Crumbs.test.mjs` is not indexed in `Servex/readme.md` either; only `processes.md:31` mentions it. Add one line to `restart.md` saying that a wrapper must copy the promisify hook, and name the test there.

With the hook copied as-is (`Servex/Crumbs.js:51`), a promisified call goes through Node's original `execFile`/`exec` and drops no breadcrumb. So `processes_async`'s PowerShell and netstat calls leave no crumb, though those slow calls are exactly what the crumb log is meant to name. A small wrapper keeps both: `cp[name][promisify.custom] = function(...a){ Crumbs.drop(...); return real[promisify.custom].apply(this, a); }`.

`Servex/Lifecycle.js:160` `typeof r === "string" ? r : r.stdout` is a second guard against a bug the Crumbs fix already removes. It is harmless, but it would hide a future regression that the test is meant to catch. Either drop it, or add a comment saying why it stays.

The change is right and small: `cp.exec` and `cp.execFile` both carry `promisify.custom` in Node 24 (checked), and only those two of the seven wrapped names have one, so the `if (real[promisify.custom])` guard is exact. `node Servex/Crumbs.test.mjs` on `worktree/qf-2` prints PASS. I did not re-run `closeout.test.mjs`. This is a Servex-only diff with no page, so it has no shots.
